title: Adding and Subtracting Fractions with the Same Denominator
seo_title: Adding and Subtracting Fractions – Primary 3 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator; solve simple word problems. (summary of the NERDC Primary 3 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 3 maths worksheets on adding and subtracting fractions with the same denominator, with pictures and simple word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Same denominator: add or subtract the tops
key_sub: The bottom number stays the same.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • When the bottom numbers (denominators) are the same, add or subtract the top numbers (numerators).
  • The bottom number does not change: 2/5 + 1/5 = 3/5.
  • A whole is 4/4, 5/5 or 6/6. To find what is left, subtract from the whole.

Examples

Example

3/8 + 2/8

3 + 2 = 5

Answer: 5/8

Example

5/6 − 4/6

5 − 4 = 1

Answer: 1/6

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the bottom numbers2/5 + 1/5 = 3/5, not 3/10.
Changing the bottom numberThe size of the parts stays the same.
Forgetting that the whole is 16/6 = 1.

faq.q: Why does the denominator stay the same?
faq.a: The parts are the same size; we only count more or fewer of them.

faq.q: Can I add 1/2 and 1/3 this way?
faq.a: No. That needs equal denominators first.

items.q: A chocolate bar has 10 equal pieces. Uju eats 410 of the bar. What fraction is left?
items.e: The whole bar is 1010. 1010 − 410 = 610 is left.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 6 equal slices. Ruth eats 16 of the pizza, then 26 more. How much does she eat altogether?
items.e: 1 + 2 = 3 sixths. The slices are still sixths, so the answer is 36, not 312.

items.q: Bisi drinks 25 of a bottle of juice. Her friend drinks 15 of the bottle. What fraction of the juice is left?

items.q: A school garden has 9 equal beds. 49 of the garden has carrots and 39 has peas. What fraction of the garden has carrots or peas?

items.q: Hadiza has 1 m of ribbon. She cuts off 310 m. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: 1 m = 1010 m. 1010 − 310 = 710 m.

items.q: There are 50 sweets in a jar. 110 of them are red. How many red sweets are there?
items.e: To find 110, divide by 10: 50 ÷ 10 = 5 sweets. It is one of 10 equal parts, so it is smaller than 50.

items.q: There are 20 pupils in a group. 310 of them walk to school. How many pupils walk to school?
items.e: First find 110: 20 ÷ 10 = 2. Then take 3 of those parts: 2 × 3 = 6 pupils.

items.q: Kemi says 27 + 37 = 514. What went wrong?
items.e: The parts are sevenths, and they stay sevenths. Add only the numerators: 2 + 3 = 5. So 27 + 37 = 57.

items.q: Zainab reads 29 of her book on Monday and 49 on Tuesday. What fraction of the book has she read?

items.q: A tower has 10 cubes. 4 cubes are red and 3 cubes are blue. The rest are white. What fraction of the tower is red or blue?
items.e: Red: 410. Blue: 310. 410 + 310 = 710.

items.q: A cake is cut into 12 equal slices. 712 of the cake is eaten at a party. What fraction is left?
items.e: The whole cake is 1212. 1212 − 712 = 512 is left.

items.q: Chioma has 38 of a pizza. Amaka has 58 of the same pizza. How much more does Amaka have?
items.e: Find the difference: 58 − 38 = 28.

items.q: Ifeanyi colours 410 of a picture in the morning and 510 after lunch. What fraction is not coloured yet?
items.e: 410 + 510 = 910 is coloured. 1010 − 910 = 110 is not coloured yet.

items.q: Bola has a ribbon 90 cm long. She cuts off 110 of it. How long is the piece she cuts off?
items.e: To find 110, divide by 10: 90 ÷ 10 = 9 cm. It is one of 10 equal parts, so it is smaller than 90.

items.q: There are 30 cubes in a box. 410 of them are red. How many red cubes are there?
items.e: First find 110: 30 ÷ 10 = 3. Then take 4 of those parts: 3 × 4 = 12 cubes.

items.q: Ife cuts a 1 m plank of wood into 10 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Each piece is 110 of 1 m: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 cm.
